notes.title: New game HASTE and some other info!
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello everyone! First off, happy 1 year anniversary to Content Warning - this time a year ago we launched CW with no idea how many people would play the game! [/h3]

We're very grateful to you all for playing Content Warning even if there haven't been many updates since launch! 🙏 It's been great seeing the mods come in from the mod support update in December. Thank you to all the modders for making such cool stuff for the community!

We've explained a bit why [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2881650/view/511817979594278722?l=english]here[/url], but for those of you who missed it: the CW team took a break from a longer project called HASTE to make Content Warning. Once CW was more stable after its launch, they had promised to come back to HASTE to finish it together with that team, which they did. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1796470/HASTE_Broken_Worlds/]HASTE is now released on Steam[/url]! 

[b]With that said, we want to manage expectations going forward regarding updates.[/b]

Content Warning is not a live-service or early access game, which means that we can't promise updates with more content. The game contains what it says on the Steam store and any additional updates are a bonus. 

The CW team is made up of 5 developers, all of whom have been working non-stop on several projects for the last couple of years. At the moment, they don't know when/if they will come back to working on Content Warning, but if they do, they will have to take a break first. If they do decide to come back and make updates for the game, we will keep you in the loop!

[b]Finding games:[/b]
If you’re having issues finding other players, we recommend checking out the [url=https://discord.gg/contentwarning]CW Discord[/url], where you can find others to play with!

[b]Ports:[/b]
We’re working with a porting studio to get the game onto other platforms, so we hope to have more news about that this year. Porting also means we will add achievements for PC!

[b]Re the video extraction issues:[/b]
In the last couple of patches, we, with your help, solved several issues that led to videos failing to extract. We want to thank everyone who sent in logs and other information to help us fix as many of these bugs as possible.

There are sadly a million things that can lead to extraction issues for the videos, some of which we have no control over on our end (like one teammate having a weird file structure on their computer) but we have done our best to fix the most common ones. If you are still having issues, please check out our [url=https://landfall.se/content-warning-faq]troubleshooting page[/url].

[b]Support:[/b]
You can find help in our [url=https://landfall.se/content-warning-faq]Content Warning FAQ[/url] for the most common issues. If you still need help, you can also reach out to support@landfall.se for troubleshooting or to ask questions about the game.

notes.title: Small update! Mod support and fixes 👻
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Hello SpöökTubers and welcome to a small update! In this patch, we have some fixes but most importantly we have added mod support via the Steam Workshop![/b][/h3]

[h3]Patch Notes: [/h3]

[b]Added[/b]
[list]
[*] Controller support (rebindable using SteamInput)
[*] Steam Workshop support for mods
[/list]
[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] A bunch of defibrillator fixes, for example not being able to speak after being rezzed
[*] Fixes related to the extraction failing when you try to get your video
[*] Expanded shadow settings allow for higher-quality shadows
[*] Made tooltips correctly display rebindable keys
[*] Made select items 1-3 rebindable
[*] Matchmaking now prioritises lower ping matches
[/list]

[h3]Why mod support?[/h3]
When we launched CW there were immediately a bunch of really cool mods being made, so we're super happy to make it possible for those mods to be on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2881650/workshop/]Steam workshop[/url]! 

The CW team is small and doesn’t have enough capacity for continuous updates alongside their other work, so having mod support is a great way to empower the community to create cool new stuff! We had hoped to have this up and running earlier but it took a little longer than expected. 

If you are a modder, here is the current documentation for creating and uploading mods: [url=https://github.com/landfallgames/ExampleCWPlugin]https://github.com/landfallgames/ExampleCWPlugin[/url]

There’s also an unofficial [url=https://discord.com/invite/yeGDSm4gFq]modding Discord [/url]you can join to find out more about Content Warning mods.

We can’t wait to see what kind of mods you all create!

[h3]Re the video extraction issues:[/h3]
In the last couple of patches we, with your help, solved several issues that led to videos failing to extract. We want to thank everyone who sent in logs and other information to help us fix as many of these bugs as possible. 

There are sadly a million things that can lead to extraction issues for the videos, some of which we have no control over on our end (like one team-mate having a weird file structure on their computer) but we have done our best to fix the most common ones. If you are still having issues after this update please reach out to our support at support@landfall.se so we can help troubleshoot. 

[h3]Future updates:[/h3]
As we spoke about in our last [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2881650/view/4370264726190091136?l=english]patch[/url], the dev-team is made up of five developers who took some time off from their main project to work on Content Warning. 

The other [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1796470/HASTE_Broken_Worlds/]project [/url]has been in the works since 2021 together with a bigger team, so it’s important to the devs that they come back to finish it. As we explained in our latest post, they won’t work more on CW during this time. Therefore, we don’t know when or if there will be more Content Warning updates. 

That said we’re very happy with what Content Warning has become! It’s been a wild ride for a six-week project that blew all of our expectations out of the water. We’re thankful to you all who have been on this journey down to the old world with us so far, and we can’t wait to see what mod support brings!

[h3]Finding games:[/h3]
If you’re having issues finding other players, we recommend checking out our Discord where you can find others to play with [url=https://discord.gg/contentwarning]https://discord.gg/contentwarning[/url]

[h3]Ports:[/h3]
We’re working with a porting studio to get the game onto other platforms, so we hope to have more news about that next year. Porting also means we will add achievements for PC!

[h3]Support:[/h3]
You can find help in our [url=https://landfall.se/content-warning-faq ]Content Warning FAQ [/url]for the most common issues if you still need help you can also reach out to support@landfall.se for help troubleshooting or to ask questions about the game.

notes.title: Content Warning proves you can give away a game for free and still make people want to buy it as it hits 1 million copies sold
notes.notes:
Turns out that you can give away a game to 6.6 million people, and still sell a ton of copies too, as that's exactly what Landfall has done with Content Warning.

Right at the start of the month, Landfall released Content Warning, a Lethal Company style game about filming your friends getting killed by cryptids, as a sort of April Fool's day bit. The best part was that it was completely free for an entire day, and that resulted in 6.6 million players picking it up. A number like that shows you how ridiculously popular the game quickly became, and now as shared by Landfall on Twitter, it seems that popularity has shown no sign of slowing down, as the game has managed to sell a further one million copies on top of having given it away for free.

That means a whole bunch of people were happy to pay for the game, which is surely a good sign for the game's future. Sure, you can have a viral hit if you're an established developer known for their funny games, but you still need to be able to make money, and it seems like Landfall will be fine in that department. The game was only made in a matter of months, and while it isn't quite as fleshed out as Lethal Company is just yet, Landfall did also promise that it has some fun updates (and fixes) on the way.

notes.title: Content Warning devs fixing mic, video and connection problems after "wild ride" of a launch
notes.notes:
It's a fond hope, a fool's hope, but perhaps 2024 will be remembered not as the year of Yet More Layoffs, but the year of Unexpected Hits. Surprise record-setters like Palworld, which I don't especially like, Helldivers 2, which I rather enjoy, and now Content Warning, which I'm still figuring out. If you missed it, the co-op horror game released on Monday with a temporary free promotion, and racked up a 200,000-player Steam concurrency last night. Published by Totally Accurate Battle Simulator outfit Landfall, it's sort of like Lethal Company in being about venturing into horrible places as a wibbly-wobbly defenceless explorer, but rather than gathering scrap for resale, you're filming yourself and the monsters in a bid to publish a viral "SpookTube" video, with tuber celebrity translating into cash for new equipment.

Each video is edited together automatically from your footage and accompanying voicechat, once you return from each trip to the Old World, and you can watch it all on an in-game monitor with a mocked-up chat feed and viewcount. It's a pungent, potted commentary on the machinations of Youtube celebrity, with heady notes of "cautionary tale about algorithmic content generation" and "cautionary tale about people endangering or hurting themselves being a dependable source of views". Urgh, I can feel an op-ed coming on. In the meantime, here's how the developers - a team of only five - are updating Content Warning following its launch success.

It's no surprise that following the success of Lethal Company (and Among Us, to some degree), another indie horror game would pop up soon to get the gaming community talking. Content Warning is that game, and just like the others we've mentioned, it's graphically simple and will run on any gaming PC from the last decade.

Content Warning doesn't demand the best graphics card, but it does want you to play with friends to make the experience better. As a co-op horror game, you're going to want up to three buddies to share the frights with.

notes.title: Oh wow!!! Content Warning is now paid after being claimed by over 6 million!
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello everyone! The last 24h have been a wild ride to say the least, never did we imagine that we would get over 200K concurrent and over 6.2 MILLION owners of the game in 24h - THANK YOU ALL SO MUCH![/h3]

It's been a real treat watching all of your videos and we are so happy that we've managed to create something that makes people have fun together. 

Now the game has gone paid - it's available for 7.99USD for those of you who didn't get it during the free promotion - for those of you who did, you get to keep the game forever!

[h3]We know there are lots of bugs and server issues, we assure you that we are working on it. [/h3]

Content Warning is made by a very small team of devs (only 5 people) so fixes may take a little while but we promise you we are doing our best to solve the issues. 

[u][b]Currently the main issues we're looking into are: [/b][/u]

⚠️Issues with voices 
⚠️Connection and hosting issues
⚠️Issues with camera footage not extracting
⚠️Issues with camera footage not being visible 

A lot of these we have leads on already and are hoping to have some fixes for tomorrow morning. 

If you have any bugs to report, crash logs to send, or other questions please reach out to support@landfall.se and we will get to you as quickly as we can. 

[b]Keep Spööking, [/b]

[b]The Content Warning Team[/b]

notes.title: Monster-filming horror game Content Warning is free to download for the next few hours
notes.notes:
If you're partial to the grim delights of Phasmophobia and not averse to the sicko enjoyments of Lethal Company, you might like new horror game Content Warning, which kind of blends the two and has the additional virtue of being free on Steam till 9am PT/5pm UK on 2nd April.

In this spooky co-op treat from Landfall Publishing, you play a bunch of amateur filmmakers - or tubers, as the kids possibly still insist on calling them - who must board a spaceship, travel to another planet and film anything monstrous they stumble on.

notes.title: Content Warning takes the internet by storm after going free on Steam
notes.notes:
Content Warning was released just yesterday, and already it's taking the internet by storm. The game launched for free and will remain so for 24 hours, leading to a shocking concurrent player peak of 86,385 as of writing.

The game, a co-op spooktacular, has you and a gaggle of friends face your fears in hopes of going viral on SpookTube. Armed with a trsuty video recorder, it's all about capturing the scariness on camera and watching it back later. The more scares you get on film, the more viral you go and the more money you get back! That money can be spent on better equipment, and the content cycle repeats again.

The game was created by Landfall Games, the minds behind Totally Accurate Battlegrounds, Stick Fight The Game, among other smaller projects. They've a history of pulling off quirky and enticing games - and it looks as though Content Warning is no different! Early reception is positive, with many taking to this cooperative horror title and having a blast messing around with its found footage spin on the genre.
